[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Lumen Technologies. Lumen traces to 1930, founded as Oak Ridge Telephone Company in Louisiana, renamed Central Telephone and Electronics in 1967, Century Telephone Enterprises in 1971, then CenturyTel, Inc., then CenturyLink, Inc., before rebranding to Lumen Technologies on September 14, 2020. It is headquartered in Monroe, Louisiana. On October 31, 2016, CenturyLink announced the acquisition of Level 3 Communications, a network and fiber company founded in 1998 as a spin-off of Kiewit Diversified Group and headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado, in a deal that closed November 1, 2017. Sources this session gave two different values for that acquisition, about 25 billion dollars per one Wikipedia article and about 34 billion dollars per another, most likely reflecting equity value versus total enterprise value including assumed debt, a common difference in how large telecom mergers are reported, though this session did not find a single source reconciling the two figures directly. Separately, and importantly for this registry, on May 2, 2017, CenturyLink completed the sale of its data centers and colocation business to BC Partners and affiliated funds for about 1.86 billion dollars, retaining a roughly 10 percent equity stake in the newly formed Cyxtera Technologies. Lumen own current colocation product page, fetched this session, still advertises 200 plus locations in North America and 120 plus cities offering colocation, suggesting Lumen retained or later rebuilt colocation infrastructure separate from what was sold in 2017, while Cyxtera own current site, also fetched this session, names only a small number of specific active United States locations, Chicago Illinois, Orange County California, and Moses Lake Washington, against a global 50 plus facilities claim, suggesting substantial change since the original 2017 divestiture. This session could not find a facility by facility record of which specific buildings were part of the 2017 sale, so whether any individual row in this registry was among the divested facilities remains an open question this session could not resolve, noted here for a future researcher rather than guessed at. This session specifically attempted reverse geocoding of this CenturyLink branded row in the Las Vegas, NV areas own stored coordinates through a third party service, throttled on 3 attempts with no usable data returned. No dedicated Lumen facility or market page was found for this location under the URL patterns tried. No address is applied.

This facility's power capacity is not published. The operator Lumen Technologies, a telecom and fiber company, divested its primary data center business to Cyxtera Technologies in 2017, retaining a roughly 10 percent stake. Whether this Las Vegas location was part of that sale or remains Lumen-operated colocation infrastructure cannot be determined from available records.

Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities of which only 2 publish power figures, totaling 10.37 MW of disclosed capacity. This facility is ranked third by published megawatts in the state, meaning the two facilities ahead of it account for the entire 10.37 MW figure, leaving this location's contribution to state totals at zero or not independently disclosed.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be assessed for relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. The address and operator attribution are verified, but no certifications, power draw, cooling capacity, or recent operational status are available from public sources. Future researchers should determine whether this address remains active and whether it belongs to Lumen's post-2017 colocation portfolio or represents a divestiture.
